interim_updates.note_text: Hatton Plantations PLC's Group revenue rose 6.1% YoY to Rs.1,790mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), but gross profit jumped 50.3% (Rs.159.8mn to Rs.240.2mn) as cost of sales grew only 2% -- gross margin expanded from 9.5% to 13.4%. By segment, Tea (98.6% of Group revenue) drove nearly all of this: Tea segment result (gross-profit level) rose from Rs.147.4mn to Rs.227.9mn (+54.6%), while the smaller Hydro Power segment was flat (Rs.12.38mn to Rs.12.32mn, -0.5%). Operating profit grew 46.9% to Rs.168.6mn as admin expenses rose only 11% and other income fell 51% (Rs.34.7mn to Rs.17.0mn, mainly lower one-off items) -- the swing was driven by the tea cost line, not overheads. Net finance costs fell 30% (Rs.13.4mn to Rs.9.4mn: finance expenses on borrowings fell from Rs.14.8mn to Rs.11.0mn as the Rs.51.4mn non-current borrowing balance at 30.06.2025 was fully repaid to nil by 30.06.2026), which flowed through to a 57% jump in PBT to Rs.159.2mn. The income tax charge more than doubled (Rs.18.3mn to Rs.47.1mn, effective rate 18.1% to 29.5%), pulling PAT growth back to 35.0% (Rs.83.1mn to Rs.112.2mn) -- tax absorbed roughly a third of the pre-tax profit gain. Working capital swung sharply negative: inventories rose Rs.495.6mn in the quarter (vs a Rs.305.5mn build in the prior-year quarter) as the Group builds tea stock ahead of the peak season, driving net cash from operations to -Rs.165.1mn (still an improvement on -Rs.515.0mn a year earlier).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for HPL -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Balance sheet and cash flow both compare cleanly against the prior-year quarter (30.06.2025), so YoY on those items is possible if added later; only P&L YoY metrics are stored here per the standard interim_updates schema.
interim_updates.takeaway: Headline growth (+35% PAT) is real and driven by the core Tea segment (gross margin nearly doubled on flat cost growth), not by one-off items -- if anything one-offs (lower other income) and a much higher effective tax rate held PAT growth back relative to the 57% PBT growth. The main caveat is working capital: a large seasonal inventory build is absorbing operating cash despite the profit improvement.
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs.1,790.4mn (+6.1% YoY); gross profit Rs.240.2mn (+50.3% YoY), gross margin 9.5% to 13.4%
Tea segment result (gross-profit level) Rs.147.4mn to Rs.227.9mn (+54.6% YoY); Hydro Power flat at Rs.12.3mn (-0.5%)
Operating profit Rs.168.6mn (+46.9% YoY); admin expenses +11% to Rs.88.6mn, other income -51% to Rs.17.0mn
Net finance costs fell 30% (Rs.13.4mn to Rs.9.4mn) as non-current borrowings were repaid to nil (from Rs.51.4mn a year earlier)
PBT +57.0% to Rs.159.2mn; tax charge more than doubled (Rs.18.3mn to Rs.47.1mn, effective rate 18.1% to 29.5%), so PAT grew a slower 35.0% to Rs.112.2mn
Net cash from operations -Rs.165.1mn (vs -Rs.515.0mn prior year) as inventories rose Rs.495.6mn in the quarter on seasonal tea stock build
key_drivers: Tea (98.6% of Group revenue): segment gross profit +54.6% YoY (Rs.147.4mn to Rs.227.9mn) on cost of sales growth of only ~2%, driving nearly all of the Group's gross-margin expansion
Hydro Power (1.4% of Group revenue): broadly flat, segment result Rs.12.38mn to Rs.12.32mn -- not a driver either way this quarter
Net finance cost swing (-30%) came from full repayment of the Rs.51.4mn non-current borrowings balance (nil at 30.06.2026 vs Rs.51.4mn a year earlier), not from lower rates
Effective tax rate rose from 18.1% to 29.5% of PBT, the single largest drag between the 57% PBT growth and the 35% PAT growth
